newsitem.title: USA: Ariz governor likely to sign clean-gas bill Monday.
newsitem.headline: Ariz governor likely to sign clean-gas bill Monday.

text.p: Arizona Governor Fife Symington is expected on Monday to sign a bill mandating the use of cleaner burning gasolines for the state by 1999, said a state environmental official.
The state legislature approved the bill (known as HP2307) last week and sent it to the governor's office on April 16.
"This is something the governor has worked long and hard for," said Sandra Kotzambasis, an official at the Arizona Department of Environmental Quality.
The bill requires the use of federal reformulated gasoline (RFG) Phase 1 gasoline by late June, with the introduction of even cleaner burning fuels in the summers of 1998 and 1999.
Last summer, the governor put together a task force to examine ways to cut down on smog-forming ozone, which was threatening to bump the state into a more serious category of clean air violators.
Refiners in California and Texas are expected to begin making RFG Phase 1 for neighboring Arizona in early May.
